segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
Hello, and welcome. This is Psalm Nights. [pause 8]

Let the day fall away. Let your jaw loosen. Let your hands rest open. [pause 11]

Tonight we read Psalm 46. It is a psalm for when the ground feels like it is moving. Mountains, waters, nations, all in an uproar. And in the middle of it, a quiet river. [pause 10]

We will read it twice. [pause 13]

verses.text: To the chief Musician for the sons of Korah, A Song upon Alamoth. God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.
Therefore will not we fear, though the earth be removed, and though the mountains be carried into the midst of the sea;
Though the waters thereof roar and be troubled, though the mountains shake with the swelling thereof. Selah.
There is a river, the streams whereof shall make glad the city of God, the holy place of the tabernacles of the most High.
God is in the midst of her; she shall not be moved: God shall help her, and that right early.
The heathen raged, the kingdoms were moved: he uttered his voice, the earth melted.
The LORD of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our refuge. Selah.
Come, behold the works of the LORD, what desolations he hath made in the earth.
He maketh wars to cease unto the end of the earth; he breaketh the bow, and cutteth the spear in sunder; he burneth the chariot in the fire.
Be still, and know that I am God: I will be exalted among the heathen, I will be exalted in the earth.
The LORD of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our refuge. Selah.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
A refuge, a strength, a help in trouble. And very present. Not far off. Not coming later. Here. [pause 14]

The psalm imagines the worst. The earth moving, the mountains falling into the sea. And then it says, therefore will not we fear. [pause 14]

Then comes a river, whose streams make glad the city of God. Not a flood. A river. Steady and quiet, while everything else roars. [pause 14]

And at the end, God speaks. Be still, and know. You do not have to fix the world tonight. You can be still. [pause 18]

A companion verse from Isaiah. [pause 12]

verses.text: Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee: because he trusteth in thee.
Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God.
And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
Perfect peace. Kept in it, by a mind that rests on him. That is not something you have to make happen. It is something you can be kept in. [pause 14]

And Paul, writing from a prison cell, tells us to bring everything to God in prayer, with thanks, and the peace of God will keep our hearts. A peace that does not have to make sense. [pause 16]

Here is Psalm 46 again. When you hear be still, let your body answer. [pause 18]

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
That is enough for tonight. [pause 8]

Let your breathing slow down on its own. In, and out. Nothing to fix, nothing to finish. [pause 12]

Whatever today was, it is over now. Tomorrow has not come yet. This is only the night, and the night belongs to God. [pause 12]

Lay down what you carried. One thing, and then another. [pause 15]

Stay here as long as you like. [pause 15]

If your mind wanders, let it wander back. There is no wrong way to rest. [pause 20]

The Lord is near. Nearer than your breath. [pause 20]

Good night. [pause 45]

first_reader.note: Written by Claude in the landing session, then Claude's pastor and cultural read.

pastor.note: Every psalm and companion is stored KJV pasted by code; reflections paraphrase in short echoes (no 8+ word typed scripture) and stay with each psalm's own point (shepherd, evening rest, keeping, shelter, stillness, quiet soul, being known, waiting, a shield in flight, light and waiting). No promise of sleep or protection: Psalm 91 says plainly it does not promise nothing hard will happen; Proverbs 3:24 framed as 'not a promise for every night'. God never quoted in first person outside scripture. Headings (Ps 3, Absalom) used only as the text's own titles.

cultural.note: Plain, unhurried English a tired woman at 11 PM can follow; no filler, no church jargon unexplained; hospital and grief named gently; shared rests vary their wording so the close is not the same sentence every night; pacing tuned only by silence (pauses) to 13.5-13.7 min voiced at the measured 117 wpm.
